title: Julia Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Print a greeting
examples.description: println prints a value followed by a newline.

examples.title: Keep a named number
examples.description: A variable gives a name to a value. The plus sign adds numbers.

examples.title: Build a message
examples.description: A dollar sign inserts a variable into a string.

examples.title: Read an array item
examples.description: Julia arrays normally start at position 1.

examples.title: Apply an action to every item
examples.description: A dot applies an operation element by element. Here each number is doubled.

examples.title: Choose an action
examples.description: if selects steps using a true-or-false rule. end closes the block.
examples.code:
score = 8
if score >= 5
 println("Pass")
else
 println("Try again")
end

examples.title: Visit a range
examples.description: 1:3 is a range including both ends. A for loop visits each value.

examples.title: Name a short calculation
examples.description: A short function definition can use an equals sign. The expression is returned.

examples.title: Use a named key
examples.description: Dict connects keys with values. The => pair operator joins a key and value.

examples.title: Group fixed values
examples.description: A tuple is a fixed group of values. You can unpack its positions into names.

examples.title: Build a list with a rule
examples.description: A comprehension makes values from inputs and an optional filter.
examples.code: println([n * 2 for n in 1:4 if n > 2])

examples.title: Group named fields
examples.description: A struct defines a type with named fields. Ordinary structs are immutable.
examples.code:
struct Book
 title::String
 pages::Int
end
book = Book("Moon Trip", 24)
println(book.pages)
